entries.name: NVIDIA Cosmos
entries.desc: World foundation model platform with a dedicated action-conditioned mode that predicts forward/inverse dynamics for robotics, camera motion, and autonomous driving.
entries.license: OpenMDW-1.1 (custom permissive license — not OSI-approved, but no field-of-use restrictions)

entries.name: Meta V-JEPA 2
entries.desc: Self-supervised video world model; the V-JEPA 2-AC variant solves robot manipulation tasks — reaching, grasping, pick-and-place — from monocular RGB with no task-specific training.

entries.name: Google DeepMind Genie 3
entries.desc: Real-time interactive world model generating explorable environments from a single text or image prompt. Described from DeepMind's own materials — there is no public source to verify this against.

entries.name: World Labs Marble
entries.desc: World Labs' first commercial world model, generating persistent, explorable 3D environments from text, image, or video input. Described from the vendor's own announcement — not independently verifiable.

entries.name: MuJoCo
entries.desc: Contact/soft-body physics engine maintained by Google DeepMind — the reference benchmark for simulation accuracy that newer GPU engines are validated against.

entries.name: Genesis
entries.desc: GPU-accelerated multi-physics engine (rigid body, FEM, MPM, particle-based) with a photorealistic renderer, purpose-built for robotics and embodied AI research.

entries.name: Bullet
entries.desc: Long-running open-source collision detection and rigid/soft-body physics engine; the basis for PyBullet and used inside Blender and Houdini.

entries.name: NVIDIA Isaac Lab
entries.desc: GPU-accelerated robot learning framework built on Isaac Sim, for large-scale parallel reinforcement learning and imitation learning.

entries.name: Project Chrono
entries.desc: Multi-physics simulation engine covering rigid/flexible bodies, granular dynamics, and fluid-structure interaction.

entries.name: Stable-Baselines3
entries.desc: Reliable PyTorch implementations of core reinforcement learning algorithms (PPO, SAC, TD3, DQN) with a consistent, well-documented interface. Stable and mature — focused on maintenance over new features.

entries.name: CleanRL
entries.desc: Single-file, research-friendly reference implementations of major RL algorithms, built for readability and reproducibility rather than production abstraction.

entries.name: Ray RLlib
entries.desc: Distributed reinforcement learning library within the Ray project, used for training at a scale beyond a single machine.

entries.name: NVIDIA Isaac Sim
entries.desc: Full robot simulation platform on Omniverse with RTX and physics-based sensor models and a built-in synthetic data generation toolset (Replicator) for training perception models.

entries.name: Open X-Embodiment
entries.desc: Google DeepMind's unified cross-embodiment robot dataset, consolidating dozens of separately collected manipulation datasets into one standardized format, alongside the RT-X model checkpoints trained on it.

entries.name: OpenAI VPT (Video PreTraining)
entries.desc: Contractor Minecraft gameplay recordings — video paired with action logs — that OpenAI used to train agents via behavioral cloning. Minecraft itself is Microsoft's IP, not licensed by OpenAI.
entries.license: MIT (code/repo); dataset freely downloadable from OpenAI's public storage

entries.name: Brax
entries.desc: Differentiable JAX-based physics engine for massively parallel simulation on accelerator hardware. Worth flagging: the project's own maintainers now recommend MuJoCo Playground for new physics-simulation work — only the training component of Brax is still actively maintained.

entries.name: Drake
entries.desc: Model-based design and verification toolkit from MIT/Toyota Research Institute — C++ dynamical-systems modeling, numerical integration, and optimization tools for robotics, broader than a pure physics engine.

entries.name: TorchRL
entries.desc: PyTorch-native reinforcement learning toolkit built around the TensorDict primitive, which passes structured data across environments, replay buffers, and policies through a shared interface.

entries.name: ManiSkill
entries.desc: GPU-parallelized robot simulation and manipulation benchmark built on SAPIEN, capable of 30,000+ FPS synthetic visual data collection on a single GPU.

entries.name: BridgeData V2
entries.desc: 60,096 real-world manipulation trajectories across 24 environments and 13 skills, collected on a low-cost WidowX 250 arm — built to study generalization across tasks and environments.
entries.license: MIT (original code/repo) / OpenMDW-1.1 (NVIDIA's LeRobot-format conversion of the data)

entries.name: Oasis
entries.desc: Interactive world model from Decart and Etched using a diffusion transformer to generate real-time, playable gameplay frame-by-frame from keyboard input — no traditional game engine involved.

entries.name: DrivingWorld
entries.desc: Video-GPT-style world model for autonomous driving, generating high-fidelity, controllable future driving video and ego-state predictions beyond 40 seconds.

entries.name: Wayve GAIA-3
entries.desc: Wayve's generative world model for autonomous driving, now at GAIA-3 (15B parameters, evolved from the original 2023 GAIA-1) — used internally to simulate safety-critical driving scenarios and evaluate vehicle policies before real-world deployment.

entries.name: Language-Table
entries.desc: Human-collected robot manipulation dataset pairing natural-language instructions with tabletop block-rearrangement demonstrations, plus a matching simulated benchmark environment for open-vocabulary language-conditioned control.

entries.name: RoboNet
entries.desc: ~162,000 manipulation trajectories (15 million frames) collected across 7 different robot platforms (Sawyer, Baxter, WidowX, Franka, Kuka, Fetch, and a Google robot) at 4 research labs, built to study cross-robot generalization.

entries.name: ABC-130K
entries.desc: 130,703 teleoperated bimanual manipulation episodes (~3,590 hours) across 195 tasks, collected on dual-arm 6-DoF robot stations by Amazon FAR, UC Berkeley, and collaborators, released with the "Scalable Behavior Cloning" paper.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 (bundles some restricted third-party checkpoints under separate terms)

entries.name: Mobile ALOHA
entries.desc: Stanford's mobile-base bimanual teleoperation platform and household manipulation demonstrations (cooking, cleaning, furniture tasks), extending the original ALOHA hardware to a mobile robot.

entries.name: CORE4D
entries.desc: 4D human-human-object interaction dataset — two people collaboratively rearranging objects, captured via motion capture for future human-robot-interaction research. Not robot data itself.

entries.name: MOSAIC
entries.desc: BAAI's large motion bank for humanoid whole-body motion tracking and teleoperation, blending optical and inertial mocap with generated motions, retargeted to the Unitree G1.

entries.name: PHUMA
entries.desc: KAIST's physics-filtered humanoid locomotion dataset, retargeting large-scale human motion capture to Unitree G1/H1-2 while correcting the physical artifacts naive retargeting introduces.

entries.name: MimicGen
entries.desc: NVIDIA and UT Austin's data-generation system that synthesizes large demonstration datasets from a small number of human demos via object-centric transform-and-replay; released sets cover 48,000+ demonstrations across 12 manipulation tasks.
entries.license: NVIDIA Source Code License (code) / CC BY 4.0 (data)

entries.name: DexMimicGen
entries.desc: Extends MimicGen's automated data-generation approach to bimanual dexterous-hand manipulation tasks.
entries.license: NVIDIA Source Code License (code) / CC BY 4.0 (data)

entries.name: RoboCasa / RoboCasa365
entries.desc: Large-scale simulation of everyday household tasks for generalist robots; RoboCasa365 expands the original 120-kitchen-scene release to 365 LLM-guided tasks, 2,500+ scenes, and 2,000+ hours of human and generated robot demonstrations.

entries.name: EgoMimic
entries.desc: Georgia Tech's method and dataset pairing Project Aria egocentric human video with matched bimanual robot teleoperation demonstrations for cross-domain imitation learning.

entries.name: EgoVerse
entries.desc: A growing egocentric human demonstration dataset for robot learning (1,362 hours, 80,000 episodes across 1,965 tasks), aggregating Project Aria captures, ALOHA teleoperation, and industry data partners.

entries.name: GRAIL
entries.desc: NVIDIA's synthetic data-generation pipeline producing physics-validated 4D human-object-interaction trajectories retargeted to the Unitree G1, covering pick-up, whole-body manipulation, sitting, and terrain traversal.

entries.name: FurnitureBench
entries.desc: KAIST CLVR lab's long-horizon furniture-assembly manipulation benchmark on a real Franka arm (plus an Isaac-Gym simulated counterpart), with 200+ hours of teleoperation data.

entries.name: ManipArena
entries.desc: A real-robot bimanual manipulation benchmark (20 tasks spanning execution reasoning, semantic reasoning, and mobile manipulation) from the CVPR 2026 Embodied AI Workshop; raw data hosted on Hugging Face in LeRobot format, with the benchmark spec and harness in the linked repo.

entries.name: UniDex
entries.desc: A robot foundation suite for universal dexterous-hand control, including 50,000+ trajectories across 8 dexterous hands retargeted from human egocentric video via human-in-the-loop retargeting.

entries.name: MimicPlay
entries.desc: Stanford and NVIDIA's hierarchical imitation-learning framework that trains a high-level planner on cheap unlabeled human "play" data and a low-level controller on a small teleoperated robot dataset.

entries.name: Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI)
entries.desc: A portable, robot-agnostic handheld gripper and data pipeline that turns in-the-wild human manipulation demonstrations into robot policies without a physical robot present during collection.

entries.name: robomimic
entries.desc: Stanford ARISE Initiative's framework and datasets (proficient-human, multi-human, and machine-generated demonstrations) for studying offline learning from robot manipulation data, spanning tasks like Lift, Can, Square, and Transport.

entries.name: CALVIN
entries.desc: University of Freiburg's benchmark for language-conditioned long-horizon manipulation — 24 hours of simulated teleoperated "play" data across 4 tabletop environments with over 20,000 language directives.

entries.name: ManiSkill2
entries.desc: SAPIEN-powered simulated manipulation benchmark with 4,000,000+ demonstration frames across 20 skill families and 2,000+ objects; the original ManiSkill2 repo has since merged into the unified ManiSkill codebase linked here.

entries.name: RoboArena
entries.desc: A distributed, real-world evaluation system for generalist robot policies built on a standardized DROID-based platform (Franka arm, Robotiq gripper, ZED cameras); episode data released as periodic dated snapshots on Hugging Face.

entries.name: LESS (Local Encoder for Spatial Sensing)
entries.desc: Technion's tactile-imaging dataset — 800+ hours of poke and palpation trajectories collected with a Franka arm and a gel-based tactile sensor on soft phantoms, paired with MRI ground truth for internal-structure reconstruction.

entries.name: EgoHumanoid (sample)
entries.desc: OpenDriveLab's sample release pairing egocentric human demonstrations (PICO VR, ZED Mini) with a smaller Unitree G1 teleoperation subset, used to co-train a VLA policy for humanoid loco-manipulation.

entries.name: PH2D
entries.desc: "Physical Human-Humanoid Data" — egocentric human task demonstrations (Apple Vision Pro, Meta Quest 3) paired with real and simulated Unitree H1 teleoperation data, used to train the Human Action Transformer.

entries.name: RoboDojo
entries.desc: A unified sim-and-real benchmark for generalist robot manipulation policies, spanning 42 Isaac Sim tasks and 18 real-world tasks across three robot embodiments.

entries.name: G1 Moves
entries.desc: 60 motion-capture-to-Unitree-G1-retargeted clips (dance and karate choreography) with exported RL policies.
entries.license: Not specified on the repo — the Hugging Face data release is CC BY 4.0

entries.name: Functional Manipulation Benchmark (FMB)
entries.desc: UC Berkeley RAIL's benchmark for diverse, contact-rich manipulation — 22,550 demonstrations of single- and multi-stage assembly tasks.
entries.license: CC BY 4.0 (data, per the project page) — no separate license declared for the repo code

entries.name: RoboCOIN
entries.desc: BAAI/FlagOpen's open bimanual manipulation dataset spanning 15 robot platforms, 421 tasks, and 180,000+ demonstrations, with roughly two-thirds of platforms being half- or full-humanoid embodiments.

entries.name: OpenHLM-data
entries.desc: Training data for whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation on the Unitree G1, combining teleoperation and human-motion-capture pipelines; raw data hosted on Hugging Face, with conversion code and pipelines in the linked repo.

entries.name: Ψ0 / psi-data
entries.desc: Training data (real-world task demos, simulated data, pretraining data) behind Ψ0, an open foundation model for universal humanoid loco-manipulation; raw data hosted on Hugging Face, with code and loaders in the linked repo.

entries.name: Humanoid Everyday
entries.desc: Unitree G1/H1 demonstrations across roughly 260 everyday household tasks (RGB, depth, and LiDAR at 30Hz, ~500GB); raw data hosted on Hugging Face, with dataloader and conversion code in the linked repo.

entries.name: Touch and Go
entries.desc: ~13,900 human touches (246,000 paired vision-tactile frames) across ~3,971 real-world objects, captured in the wild with a GelSight tactile sensor for learning cross-modal vision-touch representations.

entries.name: CMU Motion Capture Database
entries.desc: One of the oldest and most widely used motion-capture datasets in existence — 2,605 motion sequences across 6 categories from 140+ subjects, maintained by the CMU Graphics Lab on its own server since before GitHub existed.
entries.license: Free for research and commercial use (CMU's own terms); citation of NSF EIA-0196217 requested, not required

entries.name: RT-1
entries.desc: Google DeepMind's foundational robotics transformer dataset — roughly 130,000 real-robot episodes across 700+ tasks collected on 13 EDR robots, later folded into Open X-Embodiment. No dataset-owned GitHub repo; the data lives in a Google Cloud Storage bucket, and the GitHub repo (google-research/robotics_transformer) is model code only.
entries.license: Not separately stated by RT-1's own release; distributed as part of Open X-Embodiment (CC-BY data / Apache-2.0 code)

entries.name: MolmoAct Dataset
entries.desc: Ai2's real-world manipulation dataset behind MolmoAct — 10,689 trajectories on a single-arm Franka across 93 tasks (7,730 home trajectories, 2,959 tabletop trajectories), collected in-house and released in LeRobot format.

entries.name: MolmoAct2 Bimanual YAM Dataset
entries.desc: Ai2's bimanual manipulation dataset for MolmoAct2 — roughly 34,500 demonstrations (720+ hours) across 28+ tasks on a bimanual YAM robot platform.

entries.name: MolmoAct2 SO-100/101 Dataset
entries.desc: Ai2's community-sourced manipulation dataset for MolmoAct2 — 38,059 episodes (19.8M frames, ~184 hours) curated and quality-gated from 1,222 public LeRobot repos contributed by 377 users on SO-100/SO-101 arms.

entries.name: RoboMIND 2.0
entries.desc: A large Chinese cross-embodiment manipulation dataset — 310,000+ bimanual trajectories across 6 embodiments (including a TienKung humanoid) and 739 tasks.
entries.license: Apache-2.0 (per the dataset's metadata tag; the release itself ships with a near-empty card, so this is the license the org has applied rather than a detailed license clause)

entries.name: Unitree UnifoLM-WBT
entries.desc: Unitree's whole-body teleoperation dataset for the G1 humanoid, released as a collection of task-specific Hugging Face repos rather than one unified dataset artifact.

entries.name: NVIDIA GR00T X-Embodiment Sim
entries.desc: NVIDIA's simulated post-training dataset for GR00T N1 — roughly 425,000 trajectories (1.91TB) spanning cross-embodiment bimanual manipulation, humanoid tabletop manipulation, robot-arm kitchen manipulation, and Unitree G1 loco-manipulation.

entries.name: OmniRetarget
entries.desc: A human-motion-to-humanoid retargeting dataset for the Unitree G1 — about 4 hours of publicly released motion (object-interaction, terrain, and combined scenarios); the LAFAN1 source motions it also draws on can't be redistributed, so they're excluded from the public release.

entries.name: TEACh
entries.desc: Amazon's dataset of human-human interactive dialogues collected to complete household tasks inside the AI2-THOR simulator — one person plays a sighted "Commander" who can see the task, the other a "Follower" who executes it, producing paired dialogue, egocentric observations, and action sequences for training embodied agents that can both act and converse about the task.
entries.license: Code: MIT; images: Apache-2.0; dataset: CDLA-Sharing-1.0 (share-alike applies to redistributing the data itself, not to models trained on it)

entries.name: ALFRED
entries.desc: A benchmark pairing natural-language instructions and egocentric vision with expert action sequences for long-horizon household tasks in AI2-THOR, including irreversible state changes (e.g. a sliced apple can't be unsliced) that make it harder to game than simpler simulated-instruction benchmarks.

entries.name: RoboTurk
entries.desc: Stanford's crowdsourced teleoperation platform and dataset — remote workers control a real Sawyer robot arm through a web/gamified interface to produce long-horizon manipulation demonstrations (block-stacking, laundry layout, tower creation), scaling data collection beyond what a single lab can teleoperate in person.
